title: Runs: the chat's agent starts and reads perch runs through the agent gate (POST /hub/runs/a/<verb>, a runs-scoped token, the chat from agent::Caller)
operator_decision: 2026-10-08 (TRACK.md:174, the user's A + C). In this eidolon a workflow run is always its own session (eidolon/crates/cli/src/workflow.rs:3), so a run an agent starts never lands in its chat's journal. C: agents start runs THROUGH THE PERCH, on a new agent-scope route of the agent gate (today it knows only Term and Mail, perch/src/agent/mod.rs:47-73). The run is an ordinary perch run whose chat tag comes from the caller's own scoped token and socket (agent::Caller.chat, mod.rs:54-60), never from a body, a query or model text. It shows in that chat's strip (GP-a) with no extra page code, under the perch's one-browser cap and its mock-only provider, and the person answers its parks in the page. The tool the agent calls is slice PR. Not reopened here.
why:
RT gives a run a chat tag, but RT's tag is the page's claim (RT.json risk) and RT's create reads it from the request body (RT worktree state.rs:551-556 at f885903), which a model can write. An agent's runs need a route whose chat is the gate's attribution instead: peer socket, then a live door's pid, then that door's chat id (perch/src/agent/attrib.rs:1-10, perch/src/agent/token.rs:265-270). So a chat can only tag its own runs. A bash or curl child, a subagent, the TUI and a workflow run are refused (attrib.rs:18-21), so a run's own tools cannot start runs.
Today no such route exists:
- every /hub/runs/a/* path is the empty 404 of state::verb, because "a" is never a run id (perch/src/runs/state.rs:449-451, rid_ok at 174-177);
- agent_scope knows two prefixes (mod.rs:65-73).
The gate, the attribution, the start path and the one-browser cap all exist. This slice joins them without copying a check.

- Caller: `req.extensions().get::<crate::agent::Caller>().cloned()`, read before the body. Absent, or not sessions::id_ok (sessions.rs:66-73): the empty 404. This fails closed. serve sets it for every path agent_scope takes (serve.rs:378-381), and the dispatch test below keeps the two in step.
- Method: POST only, else the empty 405 (whoami's rule, token.rs:297-299).
- A query (req.uri().query() not empty): 400 "agent calls take no query: the chat is the one this tool was called from". serve keeps /hub queries (serve.rs:423-430), so this check is the handler's.
- Verbs: start, list, read. Any other verb is the empty 404. There is no answer, cancel or abandon: the person answers parks in the page (user decision).
- Bodies are a JSON object read through state::object (state.rs:489-496) under a small cap: start 4 KiB, list 64 B, read 1 KiB. Keys are strict:
  - a `chat` key: 400 "the chat is the one this tool was called from: leave chat out";
  - any other key the verb does not take: 400 naming the keys it does take (start: graph, args; list: none; read: rid, wait_s).

start {graph, args?}
1. Shape: RT's parse (graph is a string; args is an object or absent; the compact text). Args over KEEP_ARGS (2 KiB, state.rs:63-64): 400 "an agent's run takes 2 KiB of args at most". So an agent run's args are always kept on its row (state.rs:536), and the person sees what the agent asked for.
2. Admit, shared with the page: graph_name_ok, in the offered list, and <plugins>/jev/workflows/<g>.rn (state.rs:515-525). The page's offered list is --run-graphs. The agent's is agent_graphs(ctx): the names in --agent-run-graphs that are also in --run-graphs, in --run-graphs order. So:
   - the agent's list is its own flag (default wiki-hop), and it never grows when the operator widens --run-graphs for the page;
   - an agent's graph is always one the page can draw (graphs.rs:124 refuses a name outside --run-graphs).
   - Refused: 404 {error, why, graphs}, where graphs = agent_graphs(ctx), with "runs_start starts only these graphs: <names>", or "runs_start starts no graph on this perch" when the list is empty. Never the empty 404: the plugin reads that as "this perch does not know the verb" (PR).
   - No --plugins-dir or no --home: RT's 503 sentences (state.rs:519-528).
   - No chat-existence step: Caller.chat is a live door's id (sessions.rs:1110-1127), which is always known (RT's chat_known, RT-wt state.rs:617-619, could only say yes).
   Why the agent has its own list (the critics' finding, decided here). An agent's run goes unattended, with args its model picks:
   - jev's triage graphs take `ssh` or `distro` (eidolon-plugins/jev/workflows/triage-linux.rn:14-18), and triage-botforge defaults ssh to mford@127.0.0.1 (triage-botforge.rn:24);
   - their recon tools run ssh through eidolon::exec (eidolon-plugins/jev/tools/uname.rn:80), which goes straight to shell::exec with no policy asked (eidolon/crates/rune/src/host.rs:836-861);
   - the guard's ssh row is the shell tool's only (perch/src/guard/rows.rn:5-10);
   - a perch run is never yolo (proc.rs:34-36), but the installer trusts jev whole (installer/src/plugins.rs:256, the "jev" | "subagent" arm), so jev's tools run under the door's NoUser (eidolon/crates/cli/src/workflow.rs:206) with no question.
   With one shared list, an operator who adds a triage graph to --run-graphs for the page would also let a model reach another host out of sight, past D9 (BRIEF.md, operator decisions). wiki-hop is safe for an agent: its one open is https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<start>, confined to that origin (eidolon-plugins/jev/graphs/wiki-hop.json:66-69).
3. Rate, two windows over the same rows. Count the runs tagged with Caller.chat whose started_ms falls in the window:
   - the last hour, at agent_runs_hour or more: 429 {error, why} "this chat has started <N> graph runs in the last hour, the most an agent may: tell the operator rather than retrying";
   - the last 24 hours, at agent_runs_day or more: the same 429 with "in the last 24 hours".
   - agent_runs_hour defaults to 20 and agent_runs_day to 60. `--knob agent_runs_hour=<N>` and `--knob agent_runs_day=<N>` (lib.rs:171-172) are for tests.
   - The count comes from runs.json rows, so it survives a restart. It counts every run tagged with the chat, page starts beside it included.
   - Checked once, before the holder and the health probes. Two starts racing past it still meet the holder check inside begin's lock (state.rs:297-301), so the overshoot is one at most.
   - This is a rate, not a bound:
     - runs.json keeps KEPT = 500 rows and prunes the oldest ended run of ANY chat (state.rs:53, 324-330). One chat's agent at 60 a day pushes every other chat's ended runs out in about 8 days, and N such chats do it N times faster.
     - Every start leaves a run folder that the perch never removes (state.rs:31-33).
     The page's starts have both properties too. runs/README.md says so.
4. Then the shared launch, in RT's order:
   a. the cheap holder check;
   b. health::gate (perch/src/runs/health.rs:208-218);
   c. begin(home, graph, kept, Some(caller.chat)): the tag goes in the same write as the row (RT's rule), never through edit();
   d. prepare and launch (state.rs:545-555);
   e. 202 {rid, state: "running", chat}: RT's tagged answer, unchanged.
5. The agent's wording, chosen by a `Who` value the shared launch takes:
   - 409 when the holder is this chat's run: {error, why, run}, worded by the holder's state (own_busy, pure and unit-tested):
     - running: "run <rid> of this chat is still going, and there is one shared browser: wait for it with runs_read (wait_s), then start again";
     - parked: "run <rid> of this chat waits for the operator in the graph tab, and there is one shared browser: tell the operator, and do not start or read again until they say they answered or abandoned it".
     The parked wording never names runs_read. A parked run answers a read at once (read, below), so that advice would be a loop of model turns on the chat's real model, on a park that has no clock (proc.rs:30-32).
   - 409 when the holder is another chat's run, or untagged: {error, why} with "the shared browser is busy with another run: try again later, and do not retry in a loop". No rid and no chat: RT's busy() names the holder's chat (RT-wt state.rs:622-632), and another chat's agent must not learn it.
   - 503 from the health gate: its Err is dropped, and the agent is told "a service the graph runs need is down: tell the operator (the graph tab shows which)". It is never told health.rs:90's "start it with: minerva services start" (health.rs:50), a command an agent could run through bash.
   - Begin::Busy follows the same 409 rule. Io and launch failures keep RT's sentences.

list {}
- The rows tagged Caller.chat, newest first, filtered BEFORE the take (RT's rule), 20 at most (AGENT_LISTED).
- An agent row is {rid, graph, state, started_ms, ended_ms?, resumes, stopping?}: row() (state.rs:368-387) without why, exit, args and chat. Twenty of them are about 3 KB, under eidolon's 8000-character inline cap (eidolon/crates/core/src/dispatch.rs:815-817).

read {rid, wait_s?}
- rid must pass rid_ok (state.rs:174-177), else 400.
- A run that does not exist, or is not tagged Caller.chat, gets the same 404 {error, why}: "no run <rid> in this chat". It is a sentence, not the empty 404, and the same words for both, so another chat's run ids are not learned by probing.
- wait_s is an integer 0 to 60, default 0; anything else is 400. While the run is `running` and the wait lasts, the store is looked at every 250 ms (the cancel loop's pattern, state.rs:646-654), inside a tokio::select! on ctx.stop.cancelled(), so a perch stop answers at once with the state as it is. A parked or ended run answers at once. The wait does not stretch over a park: a park has no clock (proc.rs:30-32) and waits for a person, so the parked `said` tells the agent to hand over and stop reading (the critics' option (b); option (a) is in the notes).
- The answer is the agent row plus:
  - args? as stored;
  - question? and report?, each clipped to 2000 bytes on a character boundary (state.rs:197-207), with `cut: true` when one was;
  - `said`, a fixed sentence per state:
    - running: "the run is still going: read it again with wait_s to wait for it to park or end"
    - parked, `refused` not set: "the run waits for the operator's answer in the graph tab: tell them, do not answer it yourself, and do not call runs_read on it again until they say they answered"
    - parked, `refused` set: "the operator's answer could not be replayed, so this run cannot go on: ask the operator to abandon it in the graph tab, then start a new one with runs_start". This is a resume eidolon would not replay (F0 c, g and j). The run stays parked, holds the browser, and only abandon ends it (state.rs:27-29; proc.rs:521-524). agent_detail picks this sentence whenever `refused` is Some.
    - done: "the run completed: its report is below"
    - failed: "the run ended failed: the operator sees why in the graph tab. If its args left out an input the graph takes (wiki-hop: start and goal), one new runs_start with all of them is worth a try; otherwise tell the operator"
    - refused: "eidolon would not start this graph on this machine (its plugin is not trusted, enabled or loadable): tell the operator, who sees why in the graph tab, and do not start it again until they say so". It never speaks of the args, because a first-start refusal is never about them:
      - before a run exists, the door refuses only on Program::load, ensure_enabled, vouch_check and preflight (eidolon/crates/cli/src/workflow.rs:170-184), or on a setup error that main folds into `refused` (eidolon/crates/cli/src/main.rs:579);
      - args_json checks only that the args are a JSON object (workflow.rs:148-165), and RA always sends one;
      - Workflow::start checks no params (eidolon/crates/rune/src/workflow.rs:222-247); `params` is only what the door shows (:83).
      So a wrong or missing arg runs, and ends failed or done.
    - lost: "the run's process is gone and its journal has no end: tell the operator"
    - cancelled: "the operator cancelled the run"
    - abandoned: "the operator gave up on the run at its park"
- An agent answer NEVER carries:
  - out or err (detail()'s tails, state.rs:398-399; out.log holds the session's absolute path);
  - why or refused. These are eidolon's words, and its refusal hint names `eidolon plugins trust jev` (eidolon/crates/cli/src/workflow.rs:505), which the stock table allows through bash as "the harness itself" (eidolon/crates/rune/policy.rn:331-333);
  - session, eid_run or pid;
  - another chat's rid or chat.

notes:
Decisions taken here (none reopen the user's A + C):
- An own token, not term's: one token per scope (agent/mod.rs:47), so a leaked runs token opens no terminal.
- POST /hub/runs/a/<verb> under the existing gate: no routing change in serve.rs (gate at 378-381, seam at 593-595).
- Verbs start, list and read only. The person answers, cancels and abandons in the page (user decision); an agent that could answer its own run's park would defeat it.
- 409 and 503 are worded for an agent: no holder's id or chat for another chat, and no `minerva services start` (health.rs:50, 90), which bash could run.
- The agent's graph list is its own flag, --agent-run-graphs (default wiki-hop, filtered by --run-graphs), not the page's list. A shared list would let a widened --run-graphs arm unattended, model-picked ssh past D9 (start, step 2). A fixed constant was the other way; the flag keeps it the operator's to change without a code change, and its help names the risk.
- A read does not wait over a park (the critics' option (b)): the parked said and the own-chat 409 tell the agent to hand over and stop reading. Option (a), stretching wait_s over a park, would make every 60 s read one more model turn on the chat's real model for as long as the person takes, and a park has no clock (proc.rs:30-32).
- The hourly (20) and daily (60) counts and the 2 KiB args cap slow a model in a loop and keep every agent run's args on its row. They do not bound runs.json's churn (KEPT=500 is across chats, state.rs:53, 324-330) or the run folders (never removed, state.rs:33). The rate step and the README say so.
- No chat-existence check: Caller.chat is a live door's id.
- No `by` field on Run.

Answers stay under eidolon's 8000-character inline cap for tool output (eidolon/crates/core/src/dispatch.rs:815-817): 20 list rows are about 3 KB, and a read is at most 2 x 2000 clipped bytes plus the row.

The tool the agent calls is slice PR (plugins/runs, port 48147), which depends on this one. A plugin call with no token file fails in eidolon's host ("nothing is in", plugins/term/tools/list.rn:95-96 in term's copy) before anything is sent.
